data.narrative:
World Labs, a Series A–stage AI & Software company founded by Fei-Fei Li, Ben Mildenhall, Christoph Lassner, and Justin Johnson, has raised $1.23B+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable set of 9 private peers and 1 public company (Palantir), including Scale AI, Reflection AI, Physical Intelligence, Black Forest Labs, and Field AI, spanning Series A and B stages within the sector.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy base ($1.2B) and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implies a valuation of $2.5B. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $5.6B, with a range from $2.0B (Field AI) to $29.0B (Scale AI). The peer distribution reflects material dispersion in the frontier-AI subsector.

Triangulating these two methods yields a central estimate range of $2.1B (low) to $6.4B (high), with a median of $4.0B. This range reflects the tension between stage-based progression logic and observable peer valuations. Key uncertainties include whether World Labs' revenue trajectory and product maturity will track toward the lower-range peers (Physical Intelligence, Black Forest Labs) or command premiums closer to the peer median, and the extent to which Series A pricing in this sector remains volatile relative to downstream stage valuations.
